blind_target.evidence_quote: For the relationships among work engagement, job satisfaction, affective organizational commitment, and job involvement, we used the meta-analytic correlations from Newman et al. (2010). This allowed us to replicate and extend the work of Newman et al. by conducting new analyses on the same data.
blind_target.outcome_computational_quote: For example, our model produced estimated latent correlations from the A-factor of job attitudes to work engagement (φ=0.77), job satisfaction (φ=0.71), affective organizational commitment (φ=0.75), and job involvement (φ=0.72) that were identical to those reported by Newman et al. (2010). Only the RMSEA values differed slightly where our analysis yielded a value 0.006 lower than the value of 0.180 reported by Newman.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Original meta-analytic data reanalysed with variance decomposition, challenging redundancy interpretation. Original 2010 numerical model explicitly recovered up to minor fit-index variation; numerical reproduction of 2011 is not separately established. Both publications are directly re-examined; 2010 supplied the data and original numerical model, while 2011 states the challenged claim. Partial full-text extraction limits certainty, especially the scope of the 2010 robustness verdict.
blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote: Therefore, interpretation of relationships between factors such as those made by Newman et al. (2010) –and others –require analyses similar to those reported in the present study.
blind_target.title: Job attitudes and employee engagement: Considering the "A-factor".
